reviews.title: Boycott AI please!
reviews.text:
Absolutely love this app, my go to! I love looking for an identifying insects and it’s incredibly helpful when getting advice on my pet snails, isopods and spider ! The in app AI Dr Buzzy is my favourite !! I used to spend hours going on  google deep dives to find an answer but now I just need to ask dr buzzy ! The makers of this app have done an incredible job!



Update; with AI increasing and the impact it’s having on the environment, especially in contributing to the climate crisis and the endangering of bees in particular, I can no longer support it. We can’t survive without insects. I love and appreciate them so much and was so excited to have a convenient way to ask my questions. Not any more. Please, if you truly care for these amazing creatures living alongside us, remove your AI chat feature. Each search consumes a water bottle. It’s not worth it!! We only have limited amounts of drinking water ! This age of AI isn’t the new future; with it there is no future. At least for humans, I’m sure the earth will shake us off like a bad case of fleas before it reaches its end. 

Please think about my words and consider your position on generative AI and these chat features

Thank you

reviews.title: WAS great, now it’s AI slop
reviews.text:
This app used to hire horticulturist and etymologist, and the answers were excellent. 
Now it’s fed all that the horticulturists and etymologists taught them into AI, and the results are AI slop….
Worse, this app now warms the planet and disrupts bees’ and other critical pollinator’s abilities to fly, with AI data centers… That this app would choose AI slop and climate warming - THE greatest threat to critical pollinators, when the app relies on the survival of plants, insects, birds…
Also, now thy have chosen to steal jobs from horticulturists and etymologists - the very experts who made their app possible.
Whoever owns this app is horrible. Boycott AI if you care about insects, birds, plants, human survival.

reviews.title: Frustrating and Condescending
reviews.text: I briefly used this app to try to identify a handful of Lepidoptera species. Two of the IDs looked accurate, but the other two didn’t seem right. I consulted a couple other resources, including a field guide, located the species, and attempted to label my photos accordingly in the app. I wasn’t able to, and when I attempted to use the AI Assistant, the AI informed me I was wrong, despite acknowledging that the characteristics of the specimens were, in fact, consistent with the species I identified. After all that, the AI effectively told me the app wouldn’t let me manually add the correct label to the photos. Unsubscribed immediately.

reviews.title: The app is wrong about 50% of the time
reviews.text:
I take macro photographs of insects and have a decent amount of entomology experience.  This app is pretty much useless to me due to its high rate of misidentification.  For me, it’s up around 50%.  These aren’t obscure insects either, in may cases they are native Wyoming species.  I run into the same problem with identifications from around the world on iNaturalist.  The app is wrong about 50% of the time on those, too.

I see A LOT of rave reviews about how accurate this is.  It makes me wonder how other reviewers are so certain it’s accurate.  My guess is that the insect looks something like the Picture Insect photo, and therefore, it must be accurate.  

I’m not sure, but I suspect this app takes the entered photo and compares it to other photos and once it finds something similar, it identifies it.  There doesn’t seem to be any consideration about where the insect was located, the habitat, its posture, etc.  I had one his morning where it misidentified a transverse ladybug for a seven spotted ladybug.

I could be mistaken, but when I try to correct a misidentification, it only corrects it on my ID.  I don’t think it lets the developers know that the app is wrong.

If I don’t trust the app, it doesn’t do me any good.  There are much better resources available online.
